verdict: M1525 is admitted only as a source specification for a fresh address-timed replay successor over DENSE_TYPED_K8, BIT_EQUAL_SERVICE_K1X8, and BIT_TYPED_K8. It correctly freezes the ep34 checkpoint, 120-call decoder population, common 96-lane/Acc24/3-ns/240-KiB/192-B-per-cycle envelope, identical dense commits, mandatory memory/stall charges, and the prohibition on recycling M1105 cycles. This review does not authorize production execution or any cycle, traffic, speedup, energy, RTL, PPA, or Table-A claim. PRODUCT_CAPTURE_TYPED_K8 remains blocked by M1526 because M1525's optional shorthand bridge is under-specified and is not a release authority.

configuration_admission.comparison_role: equal-service cycle denominator only; frontend area is explicitly not matched and must be reported separately

fair_comparison_rules.bit_typed_k8_vs_dense_typed_k8: same resource after all mandatory charges; may become an activity-sparsity cycle ratio only after production replay

fair_comparison_rules.product_capture_vs_bit_typed_k8: not runnable until M1526 Q1-Q4 closure, exact INT8/scales, kernel/ATLIF miter, Acc24 proof, paired official AEE and a fresh independent hammer

p1_findings.evidence: An independent negative test showed build_replay_plan accepts quantization_policy=null plus four syntactically valid SHA strings and Boolean miter/bound/hammer flags, setting product_capture_ready=true.
p1_findings.impact: The optional M1525 bridge validator is not safe as a product-release authority.
p1_findings.containment: Keep PRODUCT_CAPTURE_TYPED_K8 blocked under M1526. A successor must exact-bind Q1-Q4 fields and be independently hammered before weighted replay is authored or executed.
